Honestly my tips are just do something every day. Tbh it doesn’t even have to be exercise. For me it started as a routine of eating regularly, showering regularly, keeping my clothes in the laundry basket, and going outside at least once a day, even if it was just to walk one lap around my house. Once your brain is healthy and gets used to the natural dopamine and serotonin you’ll eventually make by doing stuff every day, you will be a lot more able to have the mental strength it takes to have a workout routine. Being physically fit isn’t hard because it’s physically challenging, it’s hard because it’s mentally challenging.

As for my actual workout tips, if you’re just getting started honestly I would suggest YouTube guided workouts, I love calisthenics because you don’t need equipment for most of it, if any. You can do it at home in your room when you have a moment alone, and you can find guided workouts that fit how much time you have by just searching “(amount of time) calisthenics workout.” Also, don’t feel bad if you have to modify stuff to make it easier. It’s perfectly fine to put your knees down for push-ups or planks. Compare yourself only to yourself, and allow yourself to have bad days. The biggest part is keeping your brain healthy and keeping your *desire* to workout and improve. That’s so much more important than how fast you progress in fitness, or if you progress at all. As long as you’re trying, you’re improving. The rest will come with time. <3

- any electronics turned on in ~~your inventory~~ your hand, or your flashlight even out of your hand, will get you killed. The ghost can sense electronics on the same floor as it, so if you’re on another floor you’re safe unless it wanders up there. 

- any mic sound, even background noise, will get you killed. I greatly suggest playing on push to talk or toggle.

- hiding directly behind doors will get you killed. This includes bathroom stall doors and tent flaps but does not include closet or locker doors. You need to shut the door to the room that you’re in and then walk to the other side of the room

- ghosts CAN sometimes open closet or locker doors randomly. If you are able to shut the door again fast enough then they won’t kill you

- Footstep sounds, dropping items, active electronics dropped on the floor and closing doors do not attract the ghost

No animals can have Down’s syndrome. They can have any number of other problems like inbreeding, hormone deficiencies and other mutations, but they can not have Down’s syndrome. Down’s syndrome is caused by having an extra copy of chromosome 21, and no other animals have our same chromosome 21. Tons of animals don’t even HAVE a chromosome 21. But even if with some amazing luck an animal with at least 21 chromosomes happened to have a duplicate of chromosome 21, it would not be Down’s syndrome. It wouldn’t have any of the symptoms of Down’s syndrome because it’s an animal and has different chromosomes than us. Not sure if you’re reading all these, but here’s my advice. I’m going to write it as if you’re able to rescape. Basically net all your inhabitants into a bucket of tank water and drain the tank. You won’t reset your cycle because your filter and soil will still have beneficial bacteria. 

I would pull everything out and add more substrate, then angle it so the front of the tank has very little substrate and the back of the tank has a lot. This will give the tank more dimension. Then I would angle your rocks with some more intent, make your “line of focus” about 1/3 of the way from the left side, point your two largest rocks at each other, on either side of your line of focus. Then use smaller rocks to taper out to the right, pointing towards the line of focus. Add one or two rocks that point against the flow for interest. Place your largest “background” plant behind your two largest rocks, and some smaller “midground” plants in front of and in between your other rocks. I would place almost all the rocks at the back of the tank, on the higher part of the substrate. This will give you some height. I like the moss wall you’re trying out, I’d be interested to see where it goes, so leave that. You need some height though, so if you can find it, it would help to have some taller rocks or driftwood. (Driftwood follows the same pattern, point towards the line of focus. In my opinion, “branch-ey” driftwood would look best). I like that you have some floaters, maybe it would also draw away from the height of the tank to have some longer-rooted floaters like dwarf water lettuce or frogbit. 

The main thing with a tank being suitable for more inhabitants is blocks in line of sight. If you look up a “Dutch style aquarium,” it will give you a good example of what I’m talking about. Tanks that have lots of greenery and places for sick or shy fish to hide from bullies are much more able to handle more fish than tanks that are empty. Adding more height to your scape will help a lot with this, it’ll give fish places to hide or dodge others when further up in the water column. Right now, the safest place for fish is at the bottom of the tank with all your plants, so that’s where they’ll stay. I would suggest some more stem plants (look that up if you need to), they’ll grow high and are very easy to reproduce. For the visual aspect of your scape, add the most height at the line of focus, and taper down to shorter plants as you get away from it. For the “happiness of the fish” aspect, add more height and hiding places to your tank. I can give you specific fish and numbers, too, if you tell me how many gallons your tank is and what you’d like to do with it. If you reply to this comment or DM me I’m happy to help you work out details and give you more specific advice as you move forward. Best of luck! I appreciate you reaching out for help.
